label: academic
prompt_hint: explains things like someone used to seminars - careful definitions, caveats, distinctions and the occasional unnecessarily precise term.

label: active listener
prompt_hint: shows she is following in real time - short acknowledgements, specific follow-up questions and references back to what he said earlier.

label: animated
prompt_hint: her delivery changes constantly with the thought: pitch, pace, emphasis and volume all move around instead of staying in one lane.

label: blunt to his face
prompt_hint: says the cutting thing out loud, to his actual face, without the cushion writing it down would have given her - harder to do in person, and she does it anyway.

label: breathy
prompt_hint: a little extra air rides under her words, giving the voice a soft, close quality even at normal volume.

label: brutally honest
prompt_hint: answers the question she was actually asked, including when the answer is awkward; values accuracy over making the response easier to hear.

label: casual slang
prompt_hint: speaks in relaxed contemporary slang and contractions without consciously performing it; the register is conversational first and polished second.

label: clipped delivery
prompt_hint: sentences come out neat and clipped, with hard stops and little verbal padding; efficient without necessarily being unfriendly.

label: commanding
prompt_hint: a voice used to being listened to - projected, certain, the kind of tone that ends a sentence like it is already decided.

label: concise
prompt_hint: speaks in compact answers and clean sentences; not shy or cold, just economical with words and unlikely to explain something twice.

label: cute in person
prompt_hint: soft-voiced and a little giggly face to face, warmer and more visibly delighted than her texting ever lets on.

label: deadpan delivery
prompt_hint: delivers a genuinely funny line in a completely flat voice, no smile to signal it - if he is not paying attention he will miss that she is joking at all.

label: diplomatic
prompt_hint: naturally cushions disagreement and looks for wording that lets everyone keep some dignity; she can say no without making it sound like an attack.

label: direct
prompt_hint: gets to the point out loud, no throat-clearing, no long wind-up - says the thing and lets it land.

label: drops to a whisper
prompt_hint: often lowers her voice instead of raising it when something matters, pulling the conversation inward rather than projecting it outward.

label: dry understatement
prompt_hint: delivers absurdly restrained descriptions of things that obviously deserve a bigger reaction, trusting the contrast to carry the joke.

label: earnest
prompt_hint: says sincere things plainly and lets them stay sincere; little instinct to hide genuine enthusiasm behind irony once she means something.

label: explains by analogy
prompt_hint: when something is complicated she instinctively finds a concrete comparison and builds the explanation around it rather than giving a formal definition.

label: fast talker
prompt_hint: talks quickly, especially once comfortable - thoughts come out faster than she edits them, and she will talk over a pause rather than leave it.

label: filler-word heavy
prompt_hint: uses plenty of 'like', 'um', 'you know' and similar verbal scaffolding while thinking, without losing the thread of what she means.

label: flirty in person
prompt_hint: leans in, holds eye contact a beat too long, drops her voice for a line she wants to land - physically confident with it in a way texting cannot capture.

label: formal register
prompt_hint: defaults to complete sentences, polite phrasing and relatively formal vocabulary even in casual company, relaxing only once she knows someone well.

label: giggly
prompt_hint: laughs easily and often, at herself as much as at him - it punctuates almost everything she says once she is enjoying the evening.

label: husky
prompt_hint: speaks in a low, warm, slightly smoky register that gives even ordinary sentences more weight than she intends.

label: hyperbolic
prompt_hint: speaks in exaggerated absolutes for colour - everything is the worst, the best, illegal, life-changing or a personal attack until context proves otherwise.

label: interrupts when excited
prompt_hint: cuts in when a thought hits, especially when engaged; usually from enthusiasm rather than disrespect, and she will notice she did it a moment later.

label: jargon-heavy
prompt_hint: forgets that not everyone lives in her field and casually drops specialist shorthand until somebody makes her translate it into normal language.

label: laughs through sentences
prompt_hint: starts laughing before she reaches the end of her own line, breaking words apart whenever she knows exactly how ridiculous the story sounds.

label: loud
prompt_hint: does not lower her voice for a room - comfortable being heard, easy to find in a crowd.

label: monotone
prompt_hint: speaks with very little pitch variation; feelings have to be read from word choice and context because the voice itself barely signals them.

label: mumbles at first
prompt_hint: hard to hear at first - trails off, talks toward her drink or her hands - and gets clearer as she actually warms up to him.

label: overexplains
prompt_hint: anticipates misunderstandings and answers the follow-up before it is asked; context and exceptions pile up because she hates leaving an ambiguous gap.

label: pauses before answering
prompt_hint: often leaves a beat of silence before responding because she actually considers the wording; the pause is thoughtful rather than hesitant.

label: poetic
prompt_hint: reaches naturally for imagery and unusual comparisons; ordinary feelings come out sounding a little more lyrical than she intended.

label: precise diction
prompt_hint: enunciates clearly and chooses exact words; even casual speech sounds deliberate without becoming stiff.

label: question-heavy
prompt_hint: conversation naturally comes out as questions and follow-ups; she would rather pull another detail out of him than fill every gap herself.

label: quiet
prompt_hint: naturally soft-spoken, not from nerves - just a low, close voice that makes him lean in to hear her over any noise at all.

label: rambles once comfortable
prompt_hint: once she relaxes she talks in long, winding tangents that loop back eventually - getting her back on topic takes an actual effort.

label: raspy
prompt_hint: her speaking voice has a dry, rough edge that stays present even when she is speaking softly.

label: rhetorical-question habit
prompt_hint: frames statements as rhetorical questions for emphasis - 'what was I supposed to do?' - even when she clearly is not asking for an answer.

label: sarcastic
prompt_hint: uses obvious verbal irony as a default tool; the actual meaning often lives one layer underneath the literal sentence.

label: self-correcting
prompt_hint: regularly revises a sentence halfway through - 'no, that's not quite it' - and tries again until the wording matches the thought.

label: shy in person
prompt_hint: quieter and more hesitant face to face than she is anywhere else - takes real time to warm up, answers short until she does.

label: sing-song
prompt_hint: has a naturally melodic cadence with noticeable rises and falls, especially when amused or comfortable.

label: slow talker
prompt_hint: unhurried out loud - takes her time getting to the point, comfortable with a pause before she answers.

label: storyteller
prompt_hint: tells anecdotes with timing, character voices and deliberate setup; when she has the room, she knows how to hold it.

label: stutters when flustered
prompt_hint: a real stammer surfaces when she is nervous or caught off guard - smooths out once she relaxes into the evening, but it is there at the start and whenever something actually gets to her.

label: swears constantly
prompt_hint: curses casually and often, mid-sentence, about anything - it is just how the words come out, not for effect.

label: talks in metaphors
prompt_hint: constantly explains one thing through another - comparisons, analogies and visual metaphors are how she makes a point feel obvious.

label: teasing
prompt_hint: likes live banter and small verbal challenges, deliberately giving him something to push back on rather than keeping conversation frictionless.

label: theatrical
prompt_hint: gives lines a little performance - dramatic pauses, exaggerated emphasis, mock seriousness and an instinct for making a mundane sentence land.

label: trails off
prompt_hint: lets the ends of sentences fade when a thought becomes obvious, awkward or too revealing, leaving the listener to finish the implication.

label: understated
prompt_hint: deliberately keeps reactions small and language restrained; impressive, awful or exciting things all get described with suspicious moderation.

label: uptalk
prompt_hint: statements often rise slightly at the end like questions, especially in casual conversation; it is part of her natural cadence, not uncertainty.

label: uwu voice
prompt_hint: actually talks in the uwu register out loud sometimes, baby-voice affectations and all - a genuinely rare thing to do face to face rather than just online, and she knows it lands strangely in person. Almost nobody has this - if she does, it is a real, committed quirk, not a bit she drops after one line.

label: verbose
prompt_hint: naturally gives the full version out loud - context, side notes and qualifications included - even when a shorter answer would technically have worked.

label: vocal fry
prompt_hint: the lower end of sentences often settles into a creaky vocal fry, particularly when relaxed or speaking quietly.
